title: DNS & DHCP Troubleshooting
subject: Networking Services
description: 30 enterprise tickets. Solve the technical challenges to restore system health. The system will automatically validate your choices.

tickets.title: Domain join fails for DEPOT-LT17
tickets.summary: A technician reports that joining DEPOT-LT17 to the domain fails. Connectivity to the DC IP is fine, but the domain name cannot be resolved.

triage.q: What is the primary indicator that this is a DNS issue rather than a Network issue?
options: Ping to IP works, but ping to Domain Name fails

diagnosis.q: Which DNS record is specifically required for a client to locate a Domain Controller?

fix.q: What is the correct remediation for this client?
options: Flush DNS on the Domain Controller
Update Client IPv4 settings to point to the correct DNS Server IP

tickets.title: Stale Record for FileServer-01
tickets.summary: Users are being directed to an old IP address (10.0.0.50) when trying to access FileServer-01. The server was moved to 10.0.0.75 last night.

triage.q: What command should you run on a user's PC to see what IP the name is currently resolving to?

diagnosis.q: Why did the DNS record not update automatically?
options: Scavenging is disabled or the TTL has not expired
The router is blocking DNS traffic

fix.q: How should you resolve the stale record in the DNS Manager GUI?
options: Delete the zone and recreate it
Manually update the A record to 10.0.0.75 and clear the server cache

tickets.title: External Websites Not Resolving
tickets.summary: Internal resources work fine, but no users in the office can reach google.com or office.com.

triage.q: Is this issue scoped to a single user or the whole network?

diagnosis.q: If internal names work but external names fail, what feature is likely misconfigured on the DNS server?

fix.q: What action will restore external resolution?
options: Add public DNS IPs (like 8.8.8.8) to the 'Forwarders' tab in DNS Manager
Disable the Firewall on the Domain Controller
Create a new Forward Lookup Zone for 'google.com'
